questionText: If $p q r \neq 0$ and $p^{-x} = \frac{1}{q}, q^{-y} = \frac{1}{r}, r^{-z} = \frac{1}{p}$, what is the value of the product $x y z$?
explanation:
Given:
$p^{-x} = \frac{1}{q} = q^{-1} \implies q = p^x$
$q^{-y} = \frac{1}{r} = r^{-1} \implies r = q^y$
$r^{-z} = \frac{1}{p} = p^{-1} \implies p = r^z$

Step-by-step substitution:
Substitute $q = p^x$ into $r = q^y$:
$r = (p^x)^y = p^{x y}$

Substitute $r = p^{x y}$ into $p = r^z$:
$p = (p^{x y})^z = p^{x y z}$

Equating the exponents on both sides of $p^1 = p^{x y z}$ gives:
$x y z = 1$
